author: cnash03
text:
I didn't put the keys in the app. You chose the hosted-API option, and it already does what you want: users run on your Claude and Voyage keys without having their own, and the keys never ship in the download. What's left is deploying the API, which needs your accounts, so you'll run those steps. The Mac side is ready.

## What I changed

- **Usage cap to protect your credit.** The API has no sign-in, and its URL can be read from inside every copy of the app. So the five endpoints that call Claude are now limited to 60 requests per hour per IP address on Azure. The limit is off when you run locally. Users who hit it see a friendly "try again later" message. You can change the number in Azure without redeploying. Raise it before a class demo, because everyone on the campus network shares one IP. All 43 API tests pass, including 3 new ones for the limit.
- **`scripts/package-mac.sh <api-url>`** builds one app that runs on both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs and wraps it in `publish/mac/TaxWise.dmg`. I did a trial build and opened the `.dmg`: it holds the app for both chip types, and the file-picker permission is still there.
- **Docs:** `docs/DEPLOY.md` has the new Mac steps, and `DECISIONS.md` records this as #20.

Nothing is committed yet.

## What you run (needs your logins and keys)

1. `brew install azure-cli`, then `az login` with your Azure for Students account.
2. **Qdrant Cloud:** create a free cluster and copy its host and API key. Then load the IRS documents into it, as in `docs/DEPLOY.md` §1.
3. **Azure:** in `docs/DEPLOY.md` §2, run the commands to create the app, set your Anthropic and Voyage keys as app settings, and publish. Then check that `curl https://<app>.azurewebsites.net/health` answers.
4. **Package the Mac app:** `scripts/package-mac.sh https://<app>.azurewebsites.net`, then share `publish/mac/TaxWise.dmg`.

## What it's like for a Mac user

They open the `.dmg` and drag TaxWise into Applications. The app isn't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so the first launch is blocked. They click **Done**, go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security** and click **Open Anyway**. They only do this once. Removing that step takes an Apple Developer account ($99/year) and notarization.

## Windows, when you want it

Windows builds have to be made on Windows. There are two ways: a GitHub Actions workflow that builds on GitHub's Windows machines and attaches a `.zip` to a GitHub Release, or the one command in `DEPLOY.md` §3 run on any Windows PC. Users unzip the folder and run `TaxWise.App.exe`. Windows SmartScreen warns about the unsigned app once (**More info → Run anyway**).

Once the API is up, send me the URL and I'll commit `appsettings.Release.json` and build the `.dmg` for you.

text:
The resource group was created. The plan wasn't: your Azure for Students subscription has a quota of 0 for the free **F1** tier in Central US. The other two errors only happened because the plan didn't exist.

Two changes:

1. **Use B1 instead of F1.** `docs/DEPLOY.md` recommends B1 anyway, since F1 goes to sleep when idle and is slow to wake up. B1 is about $13/month, billed to your student credit.
2. **Pick a different app name.** App names are global across all of Azure, and `taxwise-api` is very likely already taken. Add something of your own to it.

```bash
RG=taxwise-rg
APP=taxwise-api-cnash
LOCATION=centralus

az appservice plan create -g $RG -n taxwise-plan --is-linux --sku B1 -l $LOCATION
az webapp create -g $RG -p taxwise-plan -n $APP --runtime "DOTNETCORE:10.0"
az webapp update -g $RG -n $APP --https-only true
```

If B1 also fails with a quota error, try other regions. Student subscriptions often allow only a few. This tries several and stops at the first one that works:

```bash
for LOC in eastus2 westus2 westus3 southcentralus northcentralus eastus; do
  az appservice plan create -g $RG -n taxwise-plan --is-linux --sku B1 -l $LOC && { echo "Plan created in $LOC"; break; }
done
```

Then run the `webapp create` and `webapp update` lines. You can also see which regions your subscription allows with:

```bash
az policy assignment list --query "[?contains(displayName,'location') || contains(displayName,'Location')].parameters" -o json
```

The `SyntaxWarning` lines come from the Azure CLI's own Python code and are harmless.

Once `webapp create` works, the next step is setting your keys and Qdrant details as app settings (`docs/DEPLOY.md` §2, "Secrets and settings"). Type the keys in your own terminal, not here, so they stay out of this chat and the AI logs.

text:
The app now exists at `https://taxwise-api-cnash.azurewebsites.net`. There are three steps left. Run them in the same terminal, so `RG` and `APP` are still set.

**1. Qdrant Cloud.** Skip this if you've already done it.

At https://cloud.qdrant.io, create a free cluster. Copy its host, for example `abc123.us-east4-0.gcp.cloud.qdrant.io` (no `https://` and no port), and create an API key for it. Then load the IRS documents into it:

```bash
dotnet run --project src/TaxWise.Ingestion -- --download --spot-check \
  --qdrant-host <cluster-host> --qdrant-api-key <qdrant-key>
```

The spot-check searches at the end should pass.

**2. Set your keys on the server.** Type the real values in your own terminal, not here.

```bash
az webapp config appsettings set -g $RG -n $APP -o none --settings \
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=[REDACTED] \
  Voyage__ApiKey=[REDACTED] \
  Qdrant__Host=<cluster-host> \
  Qdrant__ApiKey=[REDACTED] \
  ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production \
  ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED=true
```

**3. Publish the API and check it.**

```bash
dotnet publish src/TaxWise.Api -c Release -o publish/api
(cd publish/api && rm -f ../api.zip && zip -qr ../api.zip .)
az webapp deploy -g $RG -n $APP --src-path publish/api.zip --type zip
az webapp config set -g $RG -n $APP -o none --generic-configurations '{"healthCheckPath":"/health"}'

curl https://$APP.azurewebsites.net/health
curl -s https://$APP.azurewebsites.net/api/ask -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"question":"Is my scholarship taxable if it only paid tuition?","plainLanguage":false,"taxYear":2025}'
```

The first request after a deploy can take 30–60 seconds while the app starts.

If you get a 502, run `az webapp log tail -g $RG -n $APP`. The log line names the setting that's missing or wrong. Paste it here, with any keys removed.

Once the `/api/ask` request returns an answer citing Pub 970, tell me. I'll then run `scripts/package-mac.sh https://taxwise-api-cnash.azurewebsites.net` to build your `.dmg`, and commit the config, script, rate limit and docs on this branch.

text:
That command still had the placeholders in it. zsh reads `<anthropic-key>` as "read input from a file named anthropic-key", so nothing was sent to Azure. Each `<...>` has to be replaced with the real value.

You don't need to paste the Anthropic and Voyage keys at all. They're already in your .NET user secrets, so this reads them from there. It asks for the two Qdrant values, and nothing is printed or saved to your shell history:

```bash
RG=taxwise-rg
APP=taxwise-api-cnash

SECRETS=$(dotnet user-secrets --project src/TaxWise.Api list)
ANTHROPIC=$(echo "$SECRETS" | sed -n 's/^ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = //p')
VOYAGE=$(echo "$SECRETS" | sed -n 's/^Voyage:ApiKey = //p')
read "QHOST?Qdrant cluster host (no https://, no port): "
read -s "QKEY?Qdrant API key: "; echo

[[ -n $ANTHROPIC && -n $VOYAGE && -n $QHOST && -n $QKEY ]] || echo "A value is empty, check before continuing"

az webapp config appsettings set -g $RG -n $APP -o none --settings \
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="[REDACTED]" \
  Voyage__ApiKey="$VOYAGE" \
  Qdrant__Host="$QHOST" \
  Qdrant__ApiKey="$QKEY" \
  ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production \
  ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED=true \
  && echo "Settings saved"

unset SECRETS ANTHROPIC VOYAGE QKEY
```

To check the setting names without showing the values:

```bash
az webapp config appsettings list -g $RG -n $APP --query "[].name" -o tsv
```

You should see all six names. Then go on to step 3: publish, then the two `curl` checks.

If you haven't made the Qdrant Cloud cluster and loaded the documents into it yet (step 1), do that first. You need its host and key here.

The settings were saved, but one of them is empty. That's partly my fault: the empty-value check only printed a warning and let the save run anyway.

The most likely cause is the Qdrant key. Because the whole block was pasted at once, an extra blank line probably got read as the key's answer. This shows which value is empty, by length only, without printing any values:

```bash
az webapp config appsettings list -g $RG -n $APP \
  --query "[].{name:name, length:length(value)}" -o table
```

Whichever line shows `0`, set it again by itself. **Run each block on its own, and type or paste the value only after the prompt appears.**

If it's `Qdrant__ApiKey`:

```bash
read -s "QKEY?Qdrant API key: "; echo
[[ -n $QKEY ]] && az webapp config appsettings set -g $RG -n $APP -o none --settings Qdrant__ApiKey="$QKEY" && echo "Saved"
unset QKEY
```

If it's `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `Voyage__ApiKey`, the user-secrets lookup didn't match. Check the names (this prints names only):

```bash
dotnet user-secrets --project src/TaxWise.Api list | cut -d= -f1
```

Then send me that output.

text:
TaxWise is live and ready to share with Mac users. I checked three things:

- **API:** `https://taxwise-api-cnash.azurewebsites.net/health` answers, and a real question came back with Pub 970 citations.
- **App:** the packaged app shows the green dot, and the knowledge base loaded from Azure.
- **Installer:** `publish/mac/TaxWise.dmg` (35 MB) runs on both Apple Silicon and Intel Macs and can still open the file picker for "Upload mine."

I committed the work on `upload-my-form` as `5c9bbff`: the Azure URL setting, the usage limit, the packaging script and the docs. It isn't pushed. The AI-log files are left uncommitted for `/ai-report`.

**To share it:**
1. Send people `publish/mac/TaxWise.dmg`. A GitHub Release or a Google Drive link both work. Don't commit it; the `publish/` folder is ignored by git.
2. Tell them how to get past the first-launch block: drag TaxWise into Applications and open it. When macOS blocks it, click **Done**, then go to **System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway**. This only happens once.

**Before you share it:**
- **Set a monthly spend limit** in the Anthropic console (Settings → Limits). The 60-requests-per-hour limit is per IP address, so it slows misuse but doesn't cap your total bill.
- **Before a class demo**, raise the limit, because everyone on the Mines Wi-Fi shares one IP: `az webapp config appsettings set -g taxwise-rg -n taxwise-api-cnash --settings UsageLimit__PermitLimit=500`
- **Cost:** the B1 plan uses about $13/month of your student credit for as long as it exists. When the course is over, `az group delete -n taxwise-rg` removes everything.

**When you change things:**
- **API changes:** rerun the three publish commands from step 3. The app doesn't need rebuilding.
- **App changes:** rerun `scripts/package-mac.sh` and share the new `.dmg`.

The token in your Notes window could have been captured in this session's transcript. Change it if it's still valid.

text:
I've written it up in the repo and committed it as `3d8847e` on `upload-my-form`. Nothing is pushed yet.

**In `docs/DEPLOY.md`:**
- **What's deployed now:** a table at the top with the API URL, resource group, plan, web app and Qdrant cluster. It notes that the plan is in West US 3 because Central US had no capacity on your student account.
- **§4 Run your local App against the deployed API:** your teammate creates one file, `src/TaxWise.App/appsettings.local.json`, containing the Azure URL, and runs the App the usual way. They don't need Docker, the API or any keys. The section also explains what this can and can't test, and that their questions spend your credit and count toward the 60-per-hour limit.
- **§5 Ship API changes to Azure:** publish from `main` after a PR is merged, then check it with `curl`. It includes PowerShell versions for Windows, how to change settings and keys, logs, rolling back and re-loading the IRS documents.
- **§6 Give a teammate access:** one command you run to give them access to just `taxwise-rg`, with steps for a teammate whose school account Azure doesn't recognize.

**In the code:** the App now reads that optional `appsettings.local.json` in any build. It's gitignored, so it only affects the person who creates it. I built the App with the file and without it to confirm it switches between the Azure API and the local one.

**Small edits elsewhere:**
- `SETUP.md` now tells App-only contributors they can skip the API setup and go to §4.
- `README.md` links the new sections, and its outdated "no rate limiting" line is fixed.

**Left for you:**
- **Give your teammate access** by running the §6 command with their email.
- **`data/sources/ingest-report.json` is changed but not committed.** Your Qdrant Cloud ingestion rewrote it. Commit it if you want the cloud run recorded, or discard it with `git restore data/sources/ingest-report.json`.
- **Building the Mac app needs an extra flag here.** Debug builds fail without `-p:ValidateXcodeVersion=false`: this .NET version expects Xcode 27.1 and you have 27.2. §4 has the flag, but `SETUP.md`'s Mac run command doesn't yet.
